status_of_this_document: POST HOC protocol for labelled SENSITIVITY, POST_HOC and RECONSTRUCTION steps, declared 13 Oct 2026 on the author's decisions of 12-13 Oct 2026, after the 30 July 2026 family lock. It changes no estimator, inclusion or complete-case rule, seed, draw count, tolerance, multiplicity family, governing protocol or accepted result. None of these steps can change q90, q9 or any accepted status.

author_decision.decision: Bring the manuscript/SI analyses that run_all did not run into the package as labelled post hoc steps (Option A), add an aggregate exposure export and the H3 nested constant-versus-varying-weight test; reimplement originals exactly where they exist, label reconstructions where they do not.

primary_inference_effect: NONE: the primary families (q90 cumulative, q9 final L01-L56 DLM global tests) and every accepted status are read-only for these steps.
status_values: PASS / REVIEW / NOT_TESTED / FAIL, reported verbatim. NOT_APPLICABLE_SYNTHETIC_INPUT is used only for comparisons with study values when the input is the shipped synthetic CSV (demo); it is neutral and is never a pass of the comparison it replaces.
overall_rule: A step is FAIL if any of its statuses is FAIL; otherwise REVIEW if any status is REVIEW or NOT_TESTED; otherwise PASS. Wrapper exit codes: 0 PASS, 3 REVIEW, 4 FAIL, 1 execution failure, 2 invalid arguments.

exposure_provenance.ims: Primary IMS exposures were assigned upstream from each participant's geocoded home address by three-nearest-station inverse-distance-squared weighting, with a minimum of two valid stations.
exposure_provenance.era5: ERA5 / ERA5-HEAT exposures (air temperature, relative humidity, UTCI, MRT) were assigned upstream by bilinear interpolation.
exposure_provenance.upstream_only: Retrieval (IMS API, Copernicus CDS), geocoding and interpolation were all done upstream. The package consumes only the resulting daily histories; it never reads, stores or outputs addresses or coordinates and it does not retrieve or interpolate.

items.label: POST_HOC
items.what: H3 nested test: do the lag weights differ from constant weights? Reduced (constant weights) = outcome ~ W56 cumulative exposure + M2-L, exactly the archived CUM ... W56 ... M2_L model (rain: the archived rainy-day count; the test is invariant to dividing by 56). Full (varying weights) = the existing final L01-L56 DLM (linear exposure x natural cubic spline over lag, 3 df, internal knot 28.5, boundary knots 1 and 56, lag basis with intercept). The reduced model is the full model with a flat lag curve: 2 df.
items.pairs: the nine representative pairs: 3 outcomes x (UTCI, IMS RH, rainy-day indicator), same 55 participants and the same M2-L covariates in both models

nesting_checks.column_space: the reduced design lies in the column space of the full design (rank of the joint matrix equals the full rank; residual of the reduced exposure column on the full design <= 1e-8 relative)
nesting_checks.constrained_fit: constraining the two non-constant lag directions to zero (lag coefficients proportional to the vector a with B a = 1) reproduces the reduced fit (fitted values, RSS / deviance; relative 1e-8)
nesting_checks.on_failure: STOP: the nesting status is FAIL and no test is reported

tests.continuous: nested model-based F test with 2 and n - p_full (45) df; plus an HC3 Wald test of the 2 extra coefficients (Wald W = (C b)'(C V_HC3 C')^-1 (C b) with C spanning the complement of a; p from F(2, n - p_full) applied to W/2, the lm convention)
tests.binary: likelihood-ratio test with 2 df from the two ML deviances (both fits with the final DLM glm control, epsilon 1e-12, maxit 200)

multiplicity.rule: BH across the nine model-based p values; distinct from the existing global q9

items.run_record: H3_RUN_RECORD.json: protocol declaration (name, version, status line, SHA-256), timestamp, input SHA-256, run id, source fingerprint, nesting checks

reduced_coefficients.rule: the reduced W56 M2-L exposure coefficient (archived cumulative glm control) equals the archived CUM W56 M2_L coefficient (tolerance class cumulative)

full_global_p.rule: the full model global p equals the archived global p (tolerance class dlm)
full_global_p.table3_rule: rounded to 3 decimals; the order assumed is outcome (configuration order) x representative metric (configuration order), the order of the final DLM output

acceptance.finite: no non-finite value in the nine rows

items.manuscript_use: The manuscript cites only the recorded CSV; no number is typed by hand.

items.label: POST_HOC
items.what: nearest-station check (6 Oct 2026 analysis, reimplemented in R): 120 IMS cumulative M2-L fits (3 outcomes x 4 IMS metrics x 10 windows) and the six L01-L56 M2-L DLMs (3 outcomes x IMS RH and rainy-day indicator); the single nearest eligible station replaces IDW for the same addresses; UTCI remains ERA5
items.status: author decision 13 Oct 2026: FEATURE_ID is participant_code (ID-only check: 55/55 FEATURE_ID values equal participant_code; 0/55 for every GIS object or row ID); the raw nearest exports are read directly, with declared column aliases; no helper file and no join
items.provenance: IMS primary exposures: upstream three-nearest-station inverse-distance-squared weighting from each geocoded home address, at least two valid stations. This check: the single nearest eligible station for the same addresses replaces IDW (upstream). ERA5 / ERA5-HEAT (UTCI) unchanged (bilinear interpolation upstream). The package reads only the resulting daily histories; never addresses or coordinates.

input.kind: participant-level, local only, never published; a declared variant is identified by SHA-256 (below); a file that is not a declared variant is identified by its header line only and its provenance is REVIEW
input.layout: one long CSV: participant_code, LOCAL_DATE or JERUSALEM_LOCAL_DATE (ISO date), TD_MEAN, RH_MEAN, RAIN_TOTAL, RAIN_DAYS1; one row per participant and local date; other columns are ignored
input.alias_rule: the first alias present is used; FEATURE_ID is the participant ID field of the upstream IMS exposure tool, which was participant_code
input.date_rule: the first 10 characters must be an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) in every non-blank row, otherwise the step stops
input.lag_rule: lag k of participant i = the row dated 2026-01-29 + assessment_day_i - k (calendar anchor)
input.cumulative_rule: IMS cumulative fields rebuilt from the substituted daily histories with the declared rule (available-day means; sums)
